beats.intro: Unit nine, chapter forty-eight. [[sub]]Polynomials are built from terms, and adding them comes down to combining like terms.
beats.names: A monomial is a single term: a number, a variable, or a product of them, like thirty-eight m. [[poly]]A polynomial is one monomial or a sum of several. [[bi]]With two terms it's a binomial, [[tri]]and with three terms, a trinomial. [[sub]]Subtracting a term counts as adding a negative one, so three x squared minus two x is still a sum of two terms. [[order]]We usually write a polynomial in descending order: the highest power of x first, [[sort]]down to the number with no x.
beats.like: Like terms have the same variables raised to the same powers. [[tiles]]With algebra tiles, each kind of term has its own shape: big squares for x squared, long strips for x, small squares for ones. [[same]]Only tiles of the same shape can be counted together. [[not]]Three x squared and three x look alike, but the tiles show they are different sizes: they're not like terms.
beats.add: To add polynomials, combine like terms. [[p1]]Here's two x squared plus three x plus one, [[p2]]plus x squared minus x plus two. [[group]]Slide the tiles together by kind. [[cancel]]A positive x and a negative x make zero, so that pair cancels. [[count]]Count what's left: three x squared, plus two x, plus three. [[cols]]Lining the polynomials up in columns, like terms over like terms, does the same job without tiles.
beats.subtract: Subtracting a polynomial means subtracting every one of its terms. [[q]]Take three x squared plus two x minus one, minus the quantity x squared plus four x minus three. [[flip]]The minus sign in front of the parentheses flips the sign of every term inside: [[opp]]x squared becomes negative, four x becomes negative, and minus three becomes plus three. [[add]]Now add, as before. [[cancel]]Opposite tiles cancel in pairs. [[ans]]What's left is two x squared minus two x plus two.
beats.perim: Polynomials can describe measurements. [[rect]]A rectangle is three x plus two units long and x minus one units wide. [[walk]]Its perimeter is the distance around: length plus width plus length plus width. [[sum]]Add all four sides and combine like terms: the x terms make eight x, [[nums]]and the numbers make two. [[ans]]The perimeter is eight x plus two.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]A polynomial is a monomial or a sum of monomials, written in descending order. [[w2]]To add, combine like terms: same variables, same powers. [[w3]]To subtract, change the sign of every term being subtracted, then add. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.

beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter forty-eight, adding and subtracting polynomials.
